text:
Maya Chen: heads up — seeing repeated gRPC stream stalls between gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-34 in us-west-2. multiple training jobs drop mid-stream and then reconnect after a long backoff.

monitoring-bot: alert: grpc_stream_error_rate high on cluster/gpu-pool (5m avg 4.3%)

Samir Patel: I grabbed dmesg on node-34, kernel logs show lots of fragment reassembly failures. suspect tunnel/MTU mismatch + offload interaction.

Liam Nguyen: can you paste `ip -s link show` for the host nic and vxlan? those usually give it away.

Maya Chen: here are the quick outputs:
```
# ip link show eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
# ip link show vxlan0
45: vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default
# ethtool -k vxlan0 | grep -E "gso|gro|tso"
 gso: on
 gro: on
 tso: on
```

Maya Chen: so host NIC is jumbo 9000, CNI/vxlan is 1450. PMTU should trim, but GSO is still producing large SKBs that get fragmented on the tunnel egress.

Samir Patel: that fits. We've hit kernel tunnel GSO bugs before where large skb offloads are not split correctly for vxlan -> leads to fragment loss and gRPC streaming stalls (TCP or HTTP2 streams).

Ryan Cole: any RDMA paths affected? I know some jobs try RDMA (ib0) for intra-node comms.

Samir Patel: RDMA QPs across nodes are sometimes falling back too. It looks like the fallback stack routes over the vxlan path and hits the same fragmentation. retries spike in the ib counters.

Maya Chen: quick mitigation I applied on node-34: `sudo ethtool -K vxlan0 gso off gro off tso off` — after that gRPC streams resumed for the impacted pods.

Liam Nguyen: good quickfix. But disabling offloads on every VXLAN will increase CPU/NIC overhead. We need a durable fix: either align MTU across host and overlay, fix CNI MTU config, or upgrade kernel to the patched version.

Samir Patel: additional mitigation is to ensure MSS clamping for tunnelled TCP: add iptables rule `-m tcpmss --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` in FORWARD for clusters where tunnels exist. that prevents giant segs from being sent.

Maya Chen: can also roll a daemonset that disables offloads only on nodes serving GPU workloads as a short-term hotfix. I'll measure CPU impact in canary.

ops-bot: Created INFRA-2743: "VXLAN fragmentation causing grpc stream stalls on gpu pool" and assigned to eng-infra.

Ryan Cole: notes for the ticket: 1) reproduce with iperf and large payload gRPC stream, 2) capture tcpdump showing fragments `tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/frag.pcap host 10.0.12.34 and portrange 7100-7200`, 3) test kernel 5.15+ patches that address tunnel GSO split.

Samir Patel: FYI kernel version on affected nodes: 5.15.49. There's a backported fix in later point releases.

Liam Nguyen: action items —
- Roll daemonset hotfix to disable vxlan offloads on gpu-node* (canary 5 nodes)
- Update CNI config to set MTU to 8950 or explicitly account for vxlan overhead so host and overlay don't mismatch
- Add iptables clamp-mss to CNI postrouting or kube-proxy rules for tunnel clusters
- Plan kernel upgrade/backport for the fleet

Maya Chen: impact estimate: roughly 8% of active GPU training pods saw reconnects in last 24h; a few long-running jobs got rescheduled which bumped cloud egress and transiently increased cost. watch billing alerts during rollout.

net-telemetry-bot: suggestion: add metric for 'net_fragments_incomplete' (from /proc/net/snmp -> Frag) and alert if > 0.5% of flows per node.

Samir Patel: also think about adding flow-level fallback in grpc LB: prefer local replica if any cross-node path frag counters are high. low-effort change may improve availability before infra patch lands.

Ryan Cole: I'll stage the canary patch later today. disabling offloads has small CPU penalty on the nodes but acceptable short-term for the GPU pool.

Maya Chen: I'll attach iperf/tcpdump captures to INFRA-2743 and start the daemonset manifest. will update here when canary is live. :thumbsup:
